A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GQR research work. All 22 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison; retained equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original ViDoRe 1/2 retrieval experiments, latency measurements, reranker comparisons and method ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds ViDoRe 3 experiments, parameter sensitivity analyses, latency breakdowns and query-level case studies.

M1.justification: The GQR procedure and Algorithm 1 are unchanged: combine retrieved candidate pools, optimize the primary query embedding using KL divergence from the consensus distribution, and rank candidates with the refined embedding. Fixed hyperparameters for the new evaluation do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 retains ViDoRe 1/2 and adds ViDoRe 3 evaluation across eight subsets: cs, energy, fin_en, fin_fr, hr, industrial, pharma and physics (Table 2). This substantially expands the evaluated document corpora and domain coverage within visual document retrieval.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Average Ranking, RRF, Min-Max and Softmax score aggregation, their tuned variants, the same single retrievers and the MonoQwen2-VL-v0.1 reranker. ViDoRe 3 uses existing comparison methods; Llama-Nemo is excluded only from this newly added benchmark.

E3.justification: The original tuning protocol remains, but v2 adds evaluation on ViDoRe 3 without target-benchmark tuning, transferring a fixed GQR learning rate of 10^-4 and T=50 across six model pairs. It uses supplied markdown for that corpus and adds a T=5–100 sensitivity sweep and controlled latency measurements at T=25/50.

E4.justification: V2 adds GQR learning-rate/step sensitivity tests, component-level latency analysis, baseline fusion-weight sweeps and query-level rank trajectories (Figures 4, 5, 7 and 8). These investigate stability, computational costs and differences from score fusion. The earlier search, candidate-pool, loss and role-swapping ablations remain.

E5.justification: V2 adds standard deviations across nine retriever pairs to the retained ViDoRe 2 comparison (Table 3), and reports the same statistic across six pairs on ViDoRe 3 (Table 5). These describe configuration variability, not repeated-run uncertainty. The existing 100-run latency statement is unchanged; no new seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: The earlier result tables retain their numerical values. New ViDoRe 3 results include Colnomic/Jina at 57.4 versus its 55.7 primary baseline, and average relative gains of 2.89% for GQR versus 2.66% for Min-Max fusion. Two fin_fr entries decline by 0.1 despite the universal-improvement prose. New sensitivity curves, query trajectories and fixed-step timings add further findings.

T1.justification: The method's mathematical formulation remains unchanged, with no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation. Appendix C's added weighted-fusion equations explicitly state rules already described in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contribution: architecture-agnostic query refinement using complementary retrievers to improve retrieval efficiency and quality. The headline 14-fold speed and 54-fold memory claims remain. The broader benchmark evidence supports these retained claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 and Appendix G expand the explanation of geometry-constrained, document-dependent updates; Section 4.1 adds a latency–stability interpretation. Applicability changes from v1's explicit exclusion of zero-shot use to evidence for transferred settings. V2 removes the dedicated limitations paragraph, including its acknowledgment of missing theoretical foundations.

D1.justification: Tables 20–25 newly disclose selected GQR and fusion hyperparameters for each ViDoRe 2 model pair/subset. V2 also specifies ViDoRe 3 markdown inputs and transferred configurations. The existing optimizer, tuning grids, K=10, Docling version and code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to multimodal late interaction, dense–sparse fusion and cross-encoder-guided query refinement is substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 lightly rewrites the introduction, separates method rationale into Section 2.4, divides single-retriever and hybrid comparisons, and moves storage and selected design-choice discussions into appendices. Much of the existing prose remains verbatim; the reorganization is focused.

P2.justification: V2 adds benchmark and parameter tables, sensitivity plots, a latency breakdown and query-rank heat maps. It moves the existing architecture diagram into the main text and Algorithm 1 and the reranker plot into the appendix. The main latency plot is redrawn with direct labels and fewer displayed model series, while the hybrid comparison gains a Std column.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly depended on in-domain tuning; v2 provides substantive evidence that one transferred configuration works across six model pairs on ViDoRe 3. Sensitivity analyses, runtime decomposition and disclosed selected parameters strengthen practical validity and reproducibility. Removing explicit limitations and overstating improvement across every subset weaken qualification, but these localized shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
